name: Meadow Violet
lede: Meadow Violet is a deep, saturated reddish purple built on the landscape word *meadow*, dated by Maerz and Paul to 1928 and absent from our own painting archive entirely.

sections.title: A landscape word, a deep purple
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary records Meadow Violet as first recorded in 1928, on plate 51, row A, column 9 [1]. The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 places it in block 238, "strong purple", but only loosely, 4.9 units from that block's own center, so the fit is approximate [1]. No book held in color-kb mentions this name [4].

Despite the meadow in its name, nothing in the sources we hold ties it to a flower, grass or season; *meadow* here functions only as a family word, the way [[mauve]] or [[mushroom]] does for other names in this group [1]. Its nearest distinct named neighbor is [[hyacinth-violet]], 3.9 units away and "more vivid" by our graph's measure [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Meadow Violet is absent from our archive: zero of 23,781 paintings carry a matching patch at the usual match threshold (ΔE2000 ≤ 6, at least 5 percent of the canvas) [2]. That is a genuine absence, not a small count, and it is worth saying plainly rather than padding around it [2]. The nearest comparable colors in our data skew toward 1980s fashion purple and gem-trade "Oriental amethyst" sapphire, both outside the painting record [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[2].
